title.zh: 卷四十三 蜀書十三 黃李呂馬王張傳
title.en: Volume 43: Book of Shu 13 - Biographies of Huang, Li, Lü, Ma, Wang, and Zhang
title.raw: 卷四十三 蜀書十三 黃李呂馬王張傳 Volume 43: Book of Shu 13 - Biographies of Huang, Li, Lü, Ma, Wang, and Zhang

sentences.zh: 黃權，字公衡，巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Huang Quan, courtesy name Gongheng, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan, styled Gongheng, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，州牧劉璋召為主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; Governor Liu Zhang summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk until Yi Province Governor Liu Zhang named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時別駕張鬆建議，宜迎先主，使伐張魯。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Administrator Zhang Song proposed that it was fitting to welcome the First Sovereign and send him to campaign against Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song, Liu Zhang’s vice administrator, urged inviting Liu Bei west to attack Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 權諫曰：「左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君。

translations.literal: Quan remonstrated, saying: 'The Left General has a fierce reputation; now if we invite him and wish to treat him as retainers [buqu], we will not satisfy his heart; if we wish to receive him with the rites due a guest, then one state cannot contain two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan objected: “The Left General is famous as a fighter. Treat him like a subordinate and he will resent it; treat him as an honored guest and two masters cannot share one realm.”

sentences.zh: 若容有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。

translations.literal: If the guest has the security of Mount Tai, then the lord has the peril of piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Your guest would stand firm as Taishan while you teeter like a stack of eggs.

sentences.zh: 可但閉境，以待河清。

translations.literal: One may simply close the borders and await the river running clear [i.e. peace in the realm].
translations.idiomatic: Better seal the passes and wait until the world settles.”

sentences.zh: 」璋不聽，竟遣使迎先生，出權為廣漢長，及先主襲取益州，將帥分下郡縣。

translations.literal: ' Zhang did not listen; in the end he dispatched an envoy to welcome the lord [first sovereign]; he transferred Quan out to be chief of Guanghan; when the First Sovereign seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders fanned out into commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang refused, sent envoys to welcome Liu Bei anyway, and sidelined Huang Quan as chief of Guanghan. When Liu Bei struck, generals spread through the province.

sentences.zh: 郡縣風景附，權閉城堅守，須劉璋稽服，乃詣降先主。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties submitted like wind and shadow [swiftly]; Quan closed the city and defended firmly; he waited until Liu Zhang bowed in submission, then went to surrender to the First Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: County after county yielded; Huang Quan held his walls until Liu Zhang capitulated, then opened his gates to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主假權偏將軍。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Quan acting Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei named him acting lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：權既忠諫於主，又閉城拒守，得事君之禮。

translations.literal: 〈Xu Zhong appraises: Quan both loyally remonstrated his lord and closed the city and resisted defense—he obtained the rites of serving a lord.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu Zhong remarks that Huang Quan both warned his lord faithfully and held his city—proper conduct for a minister.

sentences.zh: 武王下車，封比干之墓，表商容之閭，所以大顯忠賢之士，而明示所貴之旨。

translations.literal: When King Wu stepped down from his chariot, he enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane—thereby greatly displaying loyal and worthy men and clearly showing the aim of what is honored.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu honored Bi Gan’s tomb and Shang Rong’s lane to proclaim loyalty—the standard Liu Bei should emulate.

sentences.zh: 先主假權將軍，善矣，然猶薄少，未足彰忠義之高節，而大勸為善者之心。〉

translations.literal: That the First Sovereign appointed Quan general is good, yet still meager—it does not suffice to display the lofty integrity of loyalty and righteousness or greatly encourage the hearts of those who do good.〉
translations.idiomatic: Promoting him to general was decent but too modest to honor such steadfast loyalty or inspire others.〉

sentences.zh: 及曹公破張魯，魯走入巴中，權進曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao defeated Zhang Lu, Lu fled into Ba-Zhong; Quan advanced his view, saying: 'If we lose Hanzhong, then the Three Ba will not flourish—this is cutting off Shu's thigh and arm.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao drove Zhang Lu into Bazhong, Huang Quan urged: “Lose Hanzhong and the Three Ba collapse—you would sever Shu’s limbs.”

sentences.zh: 」於是先主以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯，魯已還南鄭，北降曹公。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the First Sovereign appointed Quan Protector of the Army and led the various generals to welcome Lu; Lu had already returned to Nan Zheng and submitted north to Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei made Huang Quan protector of the army and marched to intercept Zhang Lu, but Zhang Lu had already doubled back to Nan Zheng and surrendered to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end [they] defeated Du Hu and Pu Hu, killed Xiahou Yuan, and occupied Hanzhong—all were Quan's original stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the victories over Du Hu and Pu Hu, the death of Xiahou Yuan, and the seizure of Hanzhong all stemmed from Huang Quan’s original plan.

sentences.zh: 後領益州刺史，徙佔河南。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yi Province and shifted to reside south of the Yellow River [in Wei territory].
translations.idiomatic: He later held titular rank as Yi inspector after submitting to Wei and living south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬宣王深器之，問權曰：「蜀中有卿輩幾人？

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Yi deeply esteemed him and asked Quan, saying: 'How many men like you, sir, are there in Shu?
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Yi thought highly of him and asked, “How many men like you remain in Shu?”

sentences.zh: 」權笑而答曰：「不圖明公見顧之重也！

translations.literal: ' Quan smiled and replied: 'I did not expect the illustrious lord to regard me so heavily!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan smiled and said, “I hardly expected such attention from you.”

sentences.zh: 」宣王與諸葛亮書曰：「黃公衡，快士也，每坐起歎述足下，不去口實。

translations.literal: ' King Xuan wrote to Zhuge Liang, saying: 'Huang Gongheng is a forthright knight; each time he sits or rises he sighs and narrates you—words do not leave his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi wrote Zhuge Liang: “Huang Gongheng is a blunt-spoken man who speaks of you whenever he rises or sits.”

sentences.zh: 」景初三年，蜀延熙二年，權遷車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: ' In the third year of Jingchu [239], the second year of Yanxi in Shu [239], Quan was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 239 Wei’s third year of Jingchu and Shu’s second year of Yanxi he became general of chariots and cavalry with Three Excellencies protocol.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：魏明帝問權：「天下鼎立，當以何地為正？

translations.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Emperor Ming of Wei asked Quan: 'The realm stands like a tripod—what place should be considered orthodox?
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shu ji records Emperor Ming asking him which regime heaven favored among the three rivals.”

sentences.zh: 」權對曰：「當以天文為正。

translations.literal: ' Quan replied: 'One should take celestial signs as orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan answered: “Heaven’s omens decide legitimacy.”

sentences.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文皇帝崩，吳、蜀二主平安，此其徵也。」〉

translations.literal: Formerly Mars lodged in the Heart [constellation] and Emperor Wen died; the two lords of Wu and Shu were safe—this is its proof.'〉
translations.idiomatic: When Mars stalled in the Heart lodger and Wei’s Emperor Wen died, the rulers of Wu and Shu were untouched—that is the proof.”〉

sentences.zh: 明年卒，謚曰景侯。

translations.literal: The next year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子邕嗣、邕無子，絕。

translations.literal: His son Yong succeeded; Yong had no son—the line ended.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huang Yong inherited but died without heirs, so the marquisate lapsed.

sentences.zh: 權留蜀子祟，為尚書郎，隨衛將軍諸葛瞻拒鄧艾。

translations.literal: Quan left behind in Shu his son Chong, who was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; he followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan to resist Deng Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan’s son Huang Chong stayed in Shu as a masters-of-writing gentleman and followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan against Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 到涪縣，瞻盤桓未近，祟屢勸瞻宜速行據險，無令敵得入平地。

translations.literal: When they reached Fu County, Zhan lingered and did not advance near; Chong repeatedly urged Zhan that he ought swiftly to march and seize defiles—do not allow the enemy to reach level ground.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuxian Zhuge Zhan hesitated; Huang Chong urged him repeatedly to seize the passes before Deng Ai reached the plain.

sentences.zh: 瞻猶與未納，祟至於流涕。

translations.literal: Zhan still dallied and did not accept; Chong reached the point of shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan still delayed until Huang Chong wept with frustration.

sentences.zh: 會艾長驅而前，瞻卻戰綿竹，祟帥厲軍士，期於必死，臨陣見殺。

translations.literal: As it happened Ai drove straight forward; Zhan withdrew to fight at Mianzhu; Chong led and exhorted the soldiers, expecting certain death; facing battle he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai swept forward; Zhuge Zhan fell back to Mianzhu. Huang Chong rallied the troops for a fight to the death and died in the front rank.

sentences.zh: 先主薨，高定恣睢於越巂，雍闓跋扈於建寧，朱褒反叛於牂牁。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign passed away, Gao Ding behaved arrogantly in Yuexi; Yong Kai acted domineeringly in Jianning; Zhu Bao rebelled in Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei’s death Gao Ding rampaged in Yuexi, Yong Kai bullied Jianning, and Zhu Bao rose in Zangke.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮南征，先由越俊，而恢案道向建寧。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang campaigned south; he first advanced through Yuexi, while Hui pressed the route toward Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang marched south through Yuexi while Li Hui drove toward Jianning.

sentences.zh: 諸縣大相糾合，圍恢軍於昆明。

translations.literal: The various counties greatly gathered and united; they surrounded Hui's army at Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: County forces united and trapped Li Hui’s army at Kunming.

sentences.zh: 時恢眾少敵倍，又未得亮聲息，繪謂南人曰：「官軍糧盡，欲規退還，吾中間久斥鄉里，乃今得旋，不能復北，欲還與汝等同計謀，故以誠相告。

translations.literal: At that time Hui's host was few, the enemy doubled; moreover he had not obtained Liang's news; he falsely told the southern men, saying: 'The official army's grain is exhausted; they plan to withdraw and return. I long ago was cast out from my native village—now I can turn back; I cannot again go north; I wish to return and join you in plotting together—therefore I tell you sincerely.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered and out of contact with Zhuge Liang, Li Hui lied to the rebels that Shu’s supplies were gone and he meant to defect south rather than march north again.”

sentences.zh: 」南人信之，故圍守怠緩。

translations.literal: ' The southern men believed him; therefore the siege defense slackened.
translations.idiomatic: They believed him and loosened the siege.

sentences.zh: 於是恢出擊，大破之，追奔逐北，南至槃江，東接牂牁，與亮聲勢相連。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui sallied forth and struck; he greatly broke them; pursuing the fleeing and chasing the north—south to the Pan River, east connecting to Zangke—he joined Liang's momentum and power in linkage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui broke out, routed them, drove the fugitives south to the Pan River and east toward Zangke, and linked up with Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 南土平定，恢軍功居多。

translations.literal: When the southern lands were pacified, Hui's army merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the south was pacified, Li Hui’s deeds ranked first.

sentences.zh: 封漢興亭侯，加安漢將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as village marquis of Hanxing and additionally appointed General Who Pacifies Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was made village marquis of Hanxing and promoted general who pacifies Han.

sentences.zh: 後軍還，南夷復叛，殺害守將。

translations.literal: Later when the army returned, the southern Yi rebelled again and killed the defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: After the army withdrew the tribes rebelled again and slew the garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 恢身往撲討，鋤盡惡類，徙其豪帥於成都，賦出叟、濮耕牛戰馬金銀犀革，充繼軍資，於時費用不乏。

translations.literal: Hui personally went to strike and punish; he extirpated the evil sorts; he relocated their powerful chieftains to Chengdu; levies produced Sou and Pu plow oxen, war horses, gold, silver, and rhinoceros hide—filling successive military supplies; at that time expenses did not lack.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui led the punitive expedition himself, uprooted the ringleaders, deported chieftains to Chengdu, and levied cattle, horses, precious metals, and hides from the Sou and Pu until the treasury stayed full.

sentences.zh: 建興七年，以交州屬吳，解恢刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jianxing [229], because Jiao Province was yielded to Wu, Hui was relieved of inspector [of Jiao].
translations.idiomatic: In 229, after Shu ceded Jiao Province to Wu, Li Hui was stripped of his inspector’s commission.

sentences.zh: 更領建寧太守，以還居本郡。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Administrator of Jianning, thereby returning to dwell in his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Jianning administrator and returned to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 徙居漢中，九年卒。

translations.literal: He moved his residence to Hanzhong; in the ninth year [231] he died.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Hanzhong and died in 231.

sentences.zh: 子遺嗣，恢弟子球，羽林右部督，隨諸葛瞻拒鄧艾，臨陣授命，死於綿竹。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded; Hui's elder brother's son Qiu was Colonel of the Right Wing of the Feathered Forest; following Zhuge Zhan he resisted Deng Ai; facing battle he gave his life and died at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Yi inherited the title; his cousin Li Qiu, colonel of the right wing of the imperial guard, followed Zhuge Zhan against Deng Ai and died fighting at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 凱答檄曰：

translations.literal: Kai replied to the proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai answered the manifesto:

sentences.zh: 天降喪亂，奸雄乘釁，天下切齒，萬國悲悼，臣妾大小，莫不思竭筋力，肝腦塗地，以除國難。

translations.literal: Heaven sent mourning and chaos; treacherous heroes seized the breach; the realm gnashed teeth; myriad states grieved; subjects great and small—none did not wish to exhaust sinew and strength, smear liver and brains on the ground, to remove the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has sent calamity; usurpers exploit every crack; all under heaven grit their teeth in grief. Every subject longs to spend sinew and blood to lift the nation’s woes.”

sentences.zh: 伏惟將軍世受漢思，以為當躬聚黨眾，率先啟行，上以報國家，下不負先人，書功竹帛，遺名千載。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the general for generations has received Han's grace; I thought you ought personally to gather hosts of supporters, take the lead and open the march—upward to repay the state, downward not to fail your forebears—inscribe merit on bamboo and silk and leave a name a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has fed on Han favor for generations—you should rally loyal hosts, march in the van, repay the dynasty above and honor your ancestors below, and win a place in the histories.”

sentences.zh: 何期臣僕吳越，背本就末乎？

translations.literal: Who expected serving as vassal to Wu and Yue—turning your back on the root and attaching to the branch?
translations.idiomatic: Who imagined you would kneel to Wu and Yue and forsake the trunk for the twig?”

sentences.zh: 昔舜勤民事，隕於蒼梧，書籍嘉之，流聲無窮。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun toiled for the people's affairs and perished at Cangwu—the writings praise him; his fame flows without end.
translations.idiomatic: Shun died on campaign at Cangwu serving the people—the classics praise him still.”

sentences.zh: 崩於江浦，何足可悲！

translations.literal: To collapse on the riverbank—what is worth grieving!
translations.idiomatic: What shame is there if he fell by the river?”

sentences.zh: 文、武受命，成王乃平。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu received the mandate; then King Cheng pacified [all].
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu took heaven’s mandate before King Cheng finished the work.”

sentences.zh: 先帝龍興，海內望風，宰臣聰睿，自天降康。

translations.literal: The Former Sovereign rose as a dragon; within the seas all looked to the wind; chief ministers were wise and keen—from Heaven came peace.
translations.idiomatic: Our late emperor rose like a dragon; the realm turned to him; wise ministers brought heaven’s blessing.”

sentences.zh: 而將軍不睹盛衰之紀，成敗之符。

translations.literal: Yet the general does not perceive the threads of rise and decline, the tokens of success and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you ignore how fortunes rise and fall.”

sentences.zh: 譬如野火在原，蹈覆河冰，火滅水泮，將何所依附？

translations.literal: It is like wildfire on the plain or treading cracking river ice—when fire dies and ice melts, where will you cling?
translations.idiomatic: You stride cracked river ice while wildfire races the plain—when both melt away, where will you stand?”

sentences.zh: 囊者將軍先君雍候，造怨而封，竇融知興，歸志世祖，皆流名後葉，世歌其美。

translations.literal: In times past the general's late father Marquis Yong—though he incurred resentment yet was enfeoffed; Dou Rong knew the rising [trend] and turned his allegiance to Emperor Guangwu—all flowed their names to later generations; the age sings their beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Your father the Yong marquis kept his fief despite old grudges; Dou Rong read the signs and joined Guangwu—posterity still sings their wisdom.”

sentences.zh: 今諸葛丞相英才挺出，深睹未萌，受遺託孤，翊贊季興，與眾無忌，錄功忘瑕。

translations.literal: Now Chancellor Zhuge's extraordinary talent stands forth; he deeply perceives what has not yet sprouted; he received the testament and was entrusted with the orphan; he wings and assists the secondary revival; with the multitude he has no avoidances; he records merit and forgets blemishes.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge’s genius reads trouble before it blooms; he accepted the late emperor’s orphan and aids our restoration; he weighs merit above old slights.”

sentences.zh: 將軍若能翻然改圖，易跡更步，古人不難追，鄙土何足宰哉！

translations.literal: If the general can suddenly change design, alter tracks and shift steps—the ancients are not hard to catch up to; how could this humble soil not suffice to govern!
translations.idiomatic: Turn your coat now, change course—you may yet rival the ancients; this frontier cannot hold you back!”

sentences.zh: 蓋聞楚國不恭，齊桓是責，夫差僭號，晉人不長。

translations.literal: I have heard that when Chu was disrespectful, Duke Huan of Qi held them responsible; when Fuchai usurped the title, the men of Jin did not endure long.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu slighted ritual, Duke Huan of Qi chastised them; when King Fuchai seized the kingly title, Jin did not survive.”

sentences.zh: 況臣與非主，誰肯歸之邪？

translations.literal: Moreover as for subjects serving a non-[legitimate] lord—who would willingly submit to him?
translations.idiomatic: Who follows a pretender willingly?”

sentences.zh: 竊惟古義，臣無越境之交，是以前後有來無往。

translations.literal: I privately consider that by ancient righteousness subjects have no diplomacy across borders—therefore formerly there were arrivals but no returns.
translations.idiomatic: Classical propriety forbids ministers from dealing across borders—hence your letters arrived unanswered.”

sentences.zh: 重承告示，發憤忘食，故略陳所懷，惟將軍察焉。

translations.literal: Again receiving your announcement, I roused zeal and forgot eating—therefore I briefly state what I harbor; may the general examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Your renewed summons stirred me past meals; I sketch my thoughts here for your judgment.”

sentences.zh: 凱威恩內著，為郡中所信，故能全其節。

translations.literal: Kai's awe-inspiring grace showed within; he was trusted by the commandery—therefore he could preserve his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai’s authority won the commandery’s trust, so he kept his honor intact.

sentences.zh: 及丞相亮南征討闓，既發在道，而闓已為高定部曲所殺。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang campaigned south to punish Kai [Yong Kai], already having set out on the road, Kai had already been killed by Gao Ding's retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang had already marched south against Yong Kai when Gao Ding’s men killed Yong Kai first.

sentences.zh: 亮至南，上表曰：「永昌郡吏呂凱、府丞王伉等，執忠絕域，十有餘年，雍闓、高定逼其東北，而凱等守義不與交通。

translations.literal: When Liang reached the south, he submitted a memorial, saying: 'Yongchang Commandery clerk Lü Kai, assistant administrator Wang Kang, and others held loyalty in a cut-off region for more than ten years; Yong Kai and Gao Ding pressed them from the northeast, yet Kai and the others guarded righteousness and did not communicate with them.
translations.idiomatic: At his arrival Zhuge Liang memorialized: “Clerk Lü Kai and assistant Wang Kang of Yongchang held loyalty in a besieged corner for ten years while Yong Kai and Gao Ding pressed them from the northeast.”

sentences.zh: 臣不意永昌風俗敦直乃爾！

translations.literal: Your servant did not expect Yongchang's customs to be so honest and upright!
translations.idiomatic: I never dreamed Yongchang’s people were so staunch!”

sentences.zh: 」以凱為雲南太守，封陽遷亭侯，會為叛夷所害，子祥嗣。

translations.literal: ' [The court] appointed Kai Administrator of Yunnan and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yangqian; as it happened he was murdered by rebel Yi; his son Xiang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai became Yunnan administrator and village marquis of Yangqian but soon fell to rebel tribes; his son Lü Xiang inherited the title.”

sentences.zh: 而王伉亦封亭侯，為永昌太守。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Kang was also enfeoffed as village marquis and became Administrator of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang too was made a village marquis and Yongchang administrator.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀世譜》曰：呂祥後為晉南夷校尉，祥子及孫世為永昌太守。

translations.literal: 〈The Shu Shifu states: Lü Xiang later became Jin Colonel of the Southern Yi; Xiang's son and grandson for generations were Administrators of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shu shifu notes that Lü Xiang later served Jin as colonel of the southern tribes and that his descendants held Yongchang for generations.”

sentences.zh: 李雄破寧州，諸呂不肯附，舉郡固守。

translations.literal: When Li Xiong broke Ning Province, the various Lüs were unwilling to submit; they raised the commandery and defended firmly.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiong took Ningzhou the Lü clan refused him and held Yongchang for the Jin court.”

sentences.zh: 王伉等亦守正節。〉

translations.literal: Wang Kang and others also guarded upright integrity.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kang and his peers kept the same steadfast loyalty.〉

sentences.zh: 王平字子均，巴西宕渠人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ping, courtesy name Zijun, was a man of Dangqu in Ba-Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping, styled Zijun, came from Dangqu in Ba-Xi.

sentences.zh: 本養外家何氏。

translations.literal: Originally he was raised by his maternal He family.
translations.idiomatic: He had been raised under the He surname on his mother’s side.

sentences.zh: 後復姓王。

translations.literal: Later he restored the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He later resumed the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 隨杜濩、樸胡詣洛陽，假校尉，從曹公征漢中，因降先主，拜牙門將、裨將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Du Hu and Pu Hu to Luoyang; he was appointed acting Colonel; he followed Duke Cao on campaign against Hanzhong; therefore he surrendered to the First Sovereign and was appointed Colonel of the Standard and General Who Supports Might.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Luoyang with Du Hu and Pu Hu as acting colonel, followed Cao Cao into Hanzhong, then defected to Liu Bei and became colonel of the standard and supporting general.

sentences.zh: 建興六年，屬參軍馬謖先鋒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing [228], he was attached to Army Adviser Ma Su's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 228 he served under army adviser Ma Su as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 謖捨水上山，舉措煩擾，平連規諫謖，謖不能用，大敗於街亭。

translations.literal: Su abandoned the water and went up the mountain; his measures were vexing and disturbed; Ping repeatedly remonstrated with Su; Su could not employ [his advice]; there was great defeat at Jieting.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Su forsook the river for the heights and bungled deployment; Wang Ping argued repeatedly but was ignored, and they were routed at Jieting.

sentences.zh: 眾盡星散，惟平所領千人鳴鼓自持，魏將張郃疑其伏兵，不往逼也。

translations.literal: The host all scattered like stars; only the thousand led by Ping beat drums and held formation; Wei general Zhang He suspected ambush and did not press forward.
translations.idiomatic: The army fled in panic while Wang Ping’s thousand men beat drums and held line until Zhang He feared an ambush and halted.

sentences.zh: 於是平徐徐收合諸營遺迸，率將士而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ping slowly gathered the scattered remnants of the various camps and led officers and troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping slowly regrouped the broken camps and marched the survivors home.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮既誅馬謖及將軍張休、李盛，奪將軍黃襲等兵。

translations.literal: After Chancellor Liang executed Ma Su as well as Generals Zhang Xiu and Li Sheng, he stripped Generals Huang Xi and others of their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang executed Ma Su, Zhang Xiu, and Li Sheng and cashiered Huang Xi’s command.

sentences.zh: 平特見崇顯，加拜參軍，統五部兼當營事，進位討寇將軍，封亭侯。

translations.literal: Ping alone was specially honored and elevated; he was additionally appointed army adviser, commanding five divisions while concurrently handling camp affairs; he advanced in rank to General Who Punishes Rebels and was enfeoffed as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping alone was rewarded with army adviser rank, command of five tribal divisions, camp duties, promotion to general who punishes rebels, and a village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 九年，亮圍祁山，平別守南圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year [231], Liang besieged Qishan; Ping separately guarded the southern enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In 231, during the Qishan siege, Wang Ping held the southern perimeter.

sentences.zh: 魏大將軍司馬宣王攻亮，張郃攻平，平堅守不動，郃不能克。

translations.literal: Wei Grand General Sima Yi attacked Liang; Zhang He attacked Ping; Ping defended firmly without moving; He could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Yi struck Zhuge Liang, Zhang He assaulted Wang Ping’s sector but could not break his defense.

sentences.zh: 十二年，亮卒於武功，軍退還，魏延作亂，一戰而敗，平之功也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year [234], Liang died at Wugong; the army withdrew; Wei Yan raised rebellion—defeated in one battle—this was Ping's merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang died at Wugong in 234 and Wei Yan mutinied on the retreat, Wang Ping crushed the revolt in a single clash.

sentences.zh: 遷後典軍、安漢將軍，副車騎將軍吳壹住漢中，又領軍漢中太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Rear Army Supervisor and General Who Pacifies Han, deputy to General of Chariots and Cavalry Wu Yi stationed in Hanzhong; he also concurrently commanded as Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to rear army supervisor and general who pacifies Han, second to Wu Yi’s chariots and cavalry command in Hanzhong, and served concurrently as Hanzhong administrator.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進封安漢侯，代壹督漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year [237], he was advanced to Marquis Who Pacifies Han and replaced Yi as supervisor of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 237 he became marquis who pacifies Han and succeeded Wu Yi as Hanzhong commander.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年，大將軍蔣琬住沔陽，平更為前護軍，署琬府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxi [238], Grand General Jiang Wan lodged at Mianyang; Ping was transferred to Forward Protector of the Army and administered Wan's headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 238, while Grand General Jiang Wan camped at Mianyang, Wang Ping became forward protector of the army and ran Jiang Wan’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，琬還住涪，拜平前監軍、鎮北大將軍，統漢中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year [243], Wan returned to lodge at Fu; Ping was appointed Forward Army Inspector and Grand General Who Guards the North, commanding Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 243, after Jiang Wan moved to Fu, Wang Ping became forward inspector and grand general who guards the north with overall authority in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 七年春，魏大將軍曹爽率步騎十餘萬向漢川，前鋒已在駱谷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year [244], Wei Grand General Cao Shuang led more than one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry toward the Han River plain; the vanguard was already at Lu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 244 Cao Shuang marched well over a hundred thousand troops toward Hanzhong with his van already through Lu Valley.

sentences.zh: 時漢中守兵不滿三萬，諸將大驚。

translations.literal: At that time Hanzhong's defending troops did not reach thirty thousand; the various generals were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than thirty thousand men held Hanzhong, and the generals panicked.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今力不足以拒敵，聽當固守漢、樂二城，遇賊令入，比爾間，涪軍足得救關。

translations.literal: Someone said: 'Now strength is insufficient to resist the enemy—we ought listen [and decide] to firmly defend Han and Le cities; meet the bandits and let them enter; in that interval Fu armies will suffice to relieve the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged abandoning the field for Han and Le cities—let Wei through while reinforcements from Fu march up to rescue the passes.”

sentences.zh: 」平曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ' Ping said: 'It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping disagreed: “No.”

sentences.zh: 漢中去涪垂千里。

translations.literal: Hanzhong is nearly a thousand li from Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong lies almost a thousand li from Fu.

sentences.zh: 賊若得關，便為禍也。

translations.literal: If the bandits obtain the passes, it becomes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If they seize the passes disaster follows.”

sentences.zh: 今宜先遣劉護軍、杜參軍據興勢，平為後拒。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting first to dispatch Protector Liu and Army Adviser Du to occupy Xingshi; Ping will be rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Send Protector Liu Min and adviser Du Qi to hold Xingshi while I cover the rear.”

sentences.zh: 若賊分向黃金，平率千人下自臨之，比爾間，涪軍行至，此計之上也。

translations.literal: If the bandits divide toward Huangjin, Ping will lead a thousand men down and personally face them—in that interval Fu armies will arrive—this plan is the uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: If they probe Huangjin I will take a thousand men downhill to pin them until the Fu relief arrives—the best plan.”

sentences.zh: 」惟護軍劉敏與平意同，即便施行。

translations.literal: ' Only Protector Liu Min agreed with Ping's intent; immediately they carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Only Protector Liu Min agreed; they acted at once.”

sentences.zh: 涪諸軍及費禕自成都相繼而至，魏軍退還，如平本策。

translations.literal: The various Fu armies and Fei Yi from Chengdu arrived one after another; Wei armies withdrew—just as in Ping's original strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fu’s columns and Fei Yi from Chengdu arrived in succession and Wei withdrew exactly as Wang Ping predicted.”

sentences.zh: 是時，鄧芝在東，馬忠在南，平在北境，咸著名跡。

translations.literal: At this time Deng Zhi was in the east, Ma Zhong in the south, Ping on the northern border—all were renowned for their traces [achievements].
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi held the east, Ma Zhong the south, Wang Ping the north—each a name to reckon with.”

sentences.zh: 平生長戎旅，手不能書，其所識不過十字，而口授作書，皆有意理。

translations.literal: Ping grew up in the army; his hand could not write; what he recognized did not exceed ten characters—yet dictating letters, all had coherent sense.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in camp, barely literate, he nonetheless dictated lucid correspondence.”

sentences.zh: 使人讀《史》、《漢》諸紀傳，聽之，備知其大義，往往論說不失其指。

translations.literal: He had others read the various annals and biographies of the Records and Han History; listening, he fully knew their great principles; often in discussion he did not miss their purport.
translations.idiomatic: He listened to readers of the *Shiji* and *Hanshu* until he grasped their themes and argued them soundly.”

sentences.zh: 遵履法度，言不戲諺，從朝至夕，端坐徹日，懷無武將之體。

translations.literal: He observed law and measure; his speech had no jest or proverb; from morning to evening he sat upright through the day—in bearing he had none of a military general's body.
translations.idiomatic: He kept regulations, avoided idle talk, and sat bolt upright from dawn to dusk—more clerk than bluff soldier.”

sentences.zh: 然性狹侵疑，為人自輕，以此為損焉。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was narrow, encroaching, and suspicious; toward others he belittled himself—thereby he suffered loss.
translations.idiomatic: Petty, jealous, and self-deprecating, he diminished his own stature.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，子訓嗣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year [248] he died; his son Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 248; his son Wang Xun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初，平同郡漢昌句

translations.literal: At first, [there was one] Gou of Hanchang in the same commandery as Ping—
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping had a fellow townsman from Hanchang surnamed Gou—

sentences.zh: 〈句古候反〉

translations.literal: 〈The surname Gou is read gou (ancient hou fan cut).〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Here the surname Gou is read like English "go" (the fanqie gloss gives an ancient *hou* reading), not like "jyu."〉

sentences.zh: 忠勇寬厚，數有戰功，功名爵位亞平，官至左將軍，封宕渠侯。

translations.literal: —loyal, brave, generous, and thick—several times meritorious in battle; his merit, fame, rank, and titles stood second to Ping; he reached Left General and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangqu.
translations.idiomatic: —named Gou Fu—who matched Wang Ping in loyalty and courage, rose to left general, and became marquis of Dangqu.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：後張翼、廖化並為大將軍，時人語曰：「前有王、句，後有張、廖。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Records of Huayang states: Later Zhang Yi and Liao Hua both became Grand Generals; people of the time said: "Before there were Wang and Gou; after there are Zhang and Liao."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Chang Qu notes that when Zhang Yi and Liao Hua became grand generals, folk rhymed: “Wang and Gou led the way; Zhang and Liao followed.”〉

sentences.zh: 張嶷字伯岐，巴郡南充國人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ni, courtesy name Boqi, was a man of Nanchongguo in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni, styled Boqi, came from Nanchong in Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷出自孤微，而少有通壯之節。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Ni came from orphan humble origins, yet in youth had forthright and stalwart integrity.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yibu tradition says he rose from poverty yet showed heroic fiber young.〉

sentences.zh: 弱冠為縣功曹。

translations.literal: At the capping age he became county merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he served as county merit officer.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀之際，山寇攻縣，縣長捐家逃亡，嶷冒白刃，攜負夫人，夫人得免。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign was settling Shu, mountain bandits attacked the county; the county chief abandoned his household and fled; Ni braved naked blades, carrying the chief's wife on his back—she escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Bei's takeover bandits stormed the county; the magistrate fled, but Zhang Ni carried his wife through sword strokes to safety.

sentences.zh: 由是顯名，州召為從事。

translations.literal: From this his name showed forth; the province summoned him as attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread and the province named him attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 時郡內士人龔祿、姚冑位二千石，當世有聲名，皆與嶷友善。

translations.literal: At that time Gentlemen Gong Lu and Yao Zhou of the commandery held two-thousand-dan rank and had renown in the generation—all were friendly with Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Local notables Gong Lu and Yao Zhou, senior officials of repute, befriended him.

sentences.zh: 建興五年，丞相亮北住漢中，廣漢綿竹山賊張慕等鈔盜軍資，劫略吏民，嶷以都尉將兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianxing [227], Chancellor Liang lodged north at Hanzhong; mountain bandits Zhang Mu and others of Mianzhu in Guanghan plundered army supplies and raided clerks and commoners; Ni as commandant led troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In 227 bandits led by Zhang Mu pillaged Mianzhu; Zhang Ni led out troops as commandant to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 嶷度其鳥散，難以戰禽。

translations.literal: Ni gauged that they would scatter like birds—hard to catch in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He judged they would melt away like a flock of birds if pursued piecemeal.

sentences.zh: 乃詐與和親，剋期置酒。

translations.literal: Therefore he falsely made peace and affinity with them, setting a date for a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: So he feigned friendship and invited them to feast.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，嶷身率左右，因斬慕等五十餘級，渠帥悉珍。

translations.literal: When wine ran deep, Ni personally led his attendants and thereupon beheaded Mu and more than fifty others; the chieftains were all wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: When they were drunk he cut down Zhang Mu and fifty followers and destroyed their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 尋其餘類，旬日清泰。

translations.literal: He tracked down the remainder of their kind; within ten days all was clear and calm.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he had cleared the hills of the rest.

sentences.zh: 後得疾病困篤，家素貧匱。

translations.literal: Later he fell gravely ill; his household had always been poor and wanting.
translations.idiomatic: A serious illness struck while his family remained destitute.

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守蜀郡何祗，名為通厚，嶷宿與疏闊，乃自輿詣祗，託以治疾。

translations.literal: He Zhi, Administrator of Guanghan from Shu Commandery, was known as accommodating and generous; though Ni had long been distant from him, [Ni] had himself carried to Zhi and entrusted him to treat the illness.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Guanghan governor He Zhi—little known to him—for medical care.

sentences.zh: 祗傾托醫療，數年除愈。

translations.literal: Zhi devoted himself to healing; after several years [Ni] was cured.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi nursed him back to health over several years.

sentences.zh: 其黨道信義皆此類也。

translations.literal: His conduct of duty and trustworthiness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his circle’s fidelity.

sentences.zh: 拜為牙門將，屬馬忠，北討汶山叛羌，南平四郡蠻夷，輒有籌畫戰克之功。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the Standard and attached to Ma Zhong; campaigning north he punished rebellious Qiang of Wenshan, pacifying south the Man and Yi of four commanderies—each time he contributed plans and victories.
translations.idiomatic: As colonel under Ma Zhong he crushed Qiang rebels in Wenshan and tribal risings in four southern commanderies with repeated tactical successes.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷受兵馬三百人，隨馬忠討叛羌。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Ni received three hundred troops and followed Ma Zhong to punish rebellious Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The tradition adds he led three hundred men under Ma Zhong against rebel Qiang.〉

sentences.zh: 嶷別督數營在先，至他裡。

translations.literal: Ni separately supervised several camps ahead, reaching Tali.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed several camps ahead to Tali.

sentences.zh: 邑所在高峻，嶷隨山立上四五里。

translations.literal: The settlement perched high and precipitous; Ni climbed four or five li along the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade stood on sheer heights four or five li up the slope.

sentences.zh: 羌於要厄作石門，於門上施床，積石於其上，過者下石槌擊之，無不糜爛。

translations.literal: The Qiang built stone gates at the choke points; on the gates they set platforms and piled stones atop—when travelers passed below they dropped stones and smashed them; none escaped pulverization.
translations.idiomatic: They barred the defiles with stone gates and dropped rocks from overhead galleries.

sentences.zh: 嶷度不可得攻，乃使譯告曉之曰：「汝汶山諸種反叛，傷害良善，天子命將討滅惡類。

translations.literal: Ni gauged that attack was impossible; therefore he sent interpreters to declare: "You peoples of Wenshan rebelled and harmed the good; the Son of Heaven ordered generals to exterminate the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no assault path, he sent interpreters: "Your Wenshan tribes rebelled and harmed innocents; the court sends armies to destroy villains."

sentences.zh: 汝等若稽顙過軍，資給糧費，福祿永隆，其報百倍。

translations.literal: If you bang foreheads and yield to the army, supplying grain and expenses, blessing and rank will flourish forever—the repayment will be a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Bow now, feed our troops, and heaven's rewards will multiply.

sentences.zh: 若終不從，大兵致誅，雷擊電下，雖追悔之，亦無益也。

translations.literal: If you finally disobey, great troops will bring execution—thunderstroke lightning—even if you repent afterward, it will avail nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse and armies will strike like lightning—too late for regrets.

sentences.zh: 」耆帥得命，即出詣嶷，給糧過軍。

translations.literal: " The elders received the command and came out to Ni, supplying grain for the army to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The headmen accepted terms, brought provisions, and let the army through.

sentences.zh: 軍前討餘種，餘種聞他裡已下，悉恐怖失所，或迎軍出降，或奔竄山谷，放兵攻擊，軍以克捷。

translations.literal: The army advanced to punish the remaining kinds; hearing Tali had fallen, they were all terrified and lost their footing—some welcomed the army and surrendered; some fled into mountain valleys; releasing troops to strike, the army thereby prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Other bands collapsed when they heard Tali had fallen—some surrendered, others fled—and Ma Zhong's force swept through.

sentences.zh: 後南夷劉冑又反，以馬忠為督庲降討冑，嶷复屬焉，戰鬥常冠軍首，遂斬冑。

translations.literal: Later the southern Yi Liu Zhou rebelled again; Ma Zhong was appointed superintendent of troops from Jiangzhou ["Kangling"] to punish Zhou; Ni again served under him—always first in combat—and thereupon beheaded Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhou rose again Ma Zhong led Jiangzhou troops with Zhang Ni in the van and took Liu Zhou's head.

sentences.zh: 平南事訖，牂牁興古獠種復反，忠令嶷領諸營往討，嶷內招降得二千人，悉傳詣漢中。〉

translations.literal: When southern pacification ended, the Lao tribes of Zangke and Xinggu rebelled again; Zhong ordered Ni to lead the camps to punish them; Ni inwardly summoned surrender of two thousand persons—all were forwarded to Hanzhong.〉
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Lao rebels in Zangke and Xinggu challenged Ma Zhong; Zhang Ni enlisted two thousand surrendered warriors and sent them to Hanzhong.〉

sentences.zh: 十四年，武都氐王苻健請降，遣將軍張尉往迎，過期不到，大將軍蔣琬深以為念。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year [246], Di king Fu Jian of Wudu requested surrender; General Zhang Wei was dispatched to welcome him; when the deadline passed and he had not arrived, Grand General Jiang Wan was deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: In 246 Di chieftain Fu Jian offered submission; Zhang Wei failed to fetch him on time, alarming Jiang Wan.

sentences.zh: 嶷平之曰：「苻健求附款至，必無他變。

translations.literal: Ni soothed him, saying: "Fu Jian sought attachment with utmost sincerity—surely there is no other change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni calmed him: "Fu Jian's pledge rings true—nothing else is afoot."

sentences.zh: 素聞健弟狡黠，又夷狄不能同功，將有乖離，是以稽留耳。

translations.literal: I have long heard Fu Jian's younger brother is crafty; moreover barbarians cannot share equal merit—there will be estrangement; therefore there is delay.
translations.idiomatic: His crafty younger brother and tribal jealousy explain the delay."

sentences.zh: 」數日，問至，健弟果將四百戶就魏，獨健來從。

translations.literal: " Several days later news arrived: Fu Jian's younger brother indeed led four hundred households to Wei—only Fu Jian came to follow Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Days later word came: most kin defected to Wei while Fu Jian alone crossed over.

sentences.zh: 初，越巂郡自丞相亮討高定之後，叟夷數反，殺太守龔祿、焦璜，是後太守不敢之郡，只住安定縣，去郡八百餘里，其郡徒有名而已。

translations.literal: At first, after Chancellor Liang punished Gao Ding, Yuexi Commandery saw repeated Sou-Yi revolts killing Administrators Gong Lu and Jiao Huang—afterward administrators dared not enter the commandery seat but lodged in Anding County, more than eight hundred li away; the commandery existed in name only.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang's southern sweep Yuexi churned with revolt; successive governors died until administration shrank to Anding, eight hundred li from the seat.

sentences.zh: 時論欲復舊郡，除嶷為越巂太守，嶷將所領往之郡，誘以恩情，蠻夷皆服，頗來降附。

translations.literal: Current debate wished to restore the old seat; Ni was appointed Administrator of Yuexi; Ni led those under his command to the seat, alluring them with kindness—the Man and Yi all submitted, quite many coming to surrender and attach.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate restored Yuexi's capital under Zhang Ni; kindness brought tribes back to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 北徼捉馬最驍勁，不承節度，嶷乃往討，生縛其帥魏狼。

translations.literal: The Zhuoma tribe on the northern frontier was fiercest and would not accept regulation; Ni therefore campaigned against them and captured alive their chief Wei Lang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuoma tribe northward refused orders until Zhang Ni seized chief Wei Lang alive.

sentences.zh: 又解縱告喻，使招懷餘類。

translations.literal: Again he released him with instruction, bidding him summon and embrace the remaining sorts.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Wei Lang to rally the rest peacefully.

sentences.zh: 表拜狼為邑侯，種落三千餘戶皆安土供職。

translations.literal: He memorialized Lang as village marquis; more than three thousand households of the tribe settled on their soil and performed duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lang became village marquis; three thousand households farmed and paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 諸種聞之，多漸降服。

translations.literal: The various kinds hearing this gradually surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread and other bands yielded.

sentences.zh: 嶷以功賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Ni for merit was granted noble rank as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni earned marquis-within-the-passes rank.

sentences.zh: 蘇祁邑君冬逢、逢弟魄渠等，已降復反。

translations.literal: The Suqi town lord Dong Feng and Feng's younger brother Po Qu had surrendered yet rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Suqi headmen Dong Feng and Po Qu rebelled after submitting.

sentences.zh: 嶷誅逢。

translations.literal: Ni executed Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni executed Dong Feng.

sentences.zh: 逢妻，旄牛王女，嶷以計原之。

translations.literal: Feng's wife was a king's daughter of Maoniu; Ni by stratagem pardoned her.
translations.idiomatic: He spared Feng's wife, a Maoniu princess, by design.

sentences.zh: 而渠逃入西徼。

translations.literal: But Qu fled into the western marches.
translations.idiomatic: Po Qu fled westward into the frontier.

sentences.zh: 渠剛猛捷悍，為諸種深所畏憚，遣所親二人詐降嶷，實取消息。

translations.literal: Qu was fierce, swift, and hardy—the various kinds deeply feared him; he dispatched two intimates feigning surrender to Ni, actually to gather intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Po Qu terrified every tribe; two agents feigned defection to spy on Zhang Ni.

sentences.zh: 嶷覺之，許以重賞，使為反間，二人遂合謀殺渠。

translations.literal: Ni perceived it; promising heavy reward he employed them as counter-spies—the two then conspired together and killed Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni bought them as double agents who murdered Po Qu.

sentences.zh: 渠死，諸種皆安。

translations.literal: When Qu died, the various kinds were all secure.
translations.idiomatic: His death restored calm.

sentences.zh: 又斯都耆帥李求承昔手殺龔祿，嶷求募捕得，數其宿惡而誅之。

translations.literal: Moreover Sidu elder Li Qiucheng had personally killed Gong Lu long ago; Ni sought bounty hunters who seized him, enumerated his old crimes, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted down Sidu chief Li Qiucheng for Gong Lu's murder and executed him after listing crimes.

sentences.zh: 始嶷以郡郛宇頹壞，更築小塢。

translations.literal: At first Ni because the commandery walls were ruined built a small walled redoubt.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the county walls ruinous he first threw up a small fortress.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，徙還故郡，繕治城郭，夷種男女莫不致力。』

translations.literal: After three years in office he moved back to the old seat, repairing walls and moats—men and women of the Yi tribes all exerted strength.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he returned to the old capital and rebuilt it with tribal labor.

sentences.zh: 定莋、台登、卑水三縣去郡三百餘里，舊出鹽鐵及漆，而夷徼久自固食。

translations.literal: The three counties Dingzuo, Taideng, and Beishui lay over three hundred li from the commandery seat; formerly they produced salt, iron, and lacquer, yet the Yi marches long monopolized them for their own food.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzuo, Taideng, and Beishui—salt, iron, and lacquer heartlands three hundred li out—had been hoarded by frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 嶷率所領奪取，署長吏焉。

translations.literal: Ni led his command to seize them and appointed chief clerks there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni seized the districts and installed magistrates.

sentences.zh: 嶷之到定莋，定莋率豪狼岑，盤木王舅，甚為蠻夷所信任，忿嶷自侵，不自來詣。

translations.literal: When Ni reached Dingzuo, the Dingzuo chief Lang Cen—uncle by marriage of the king of Panmu—was deeply trusted by the Man and Yi; resenting Ni's intrusion he did not come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Lang Cen, kin to the Panmu king, snubbed Zhang Ni's arrival.

sentences.zh: 嶷使壯士數十直往收致，撻而殺之，持屍還種，厚加賞賜。

translations.literal: Ni sent several dozen stalwarts straight to seize him, flogged and killed him, carried the corpse back to their tribe, and richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni arrested Lang Cen, executed him publicly, returned the body with gifts, and cowed the clan.

sentences.zh: 喻以狼岑之惡，且曰：「無得妄動，動即殄矣！

translations.literal: He explained Lang Cen's wickedness and said: "Do not rashly move—if you move you will be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: He lectured them on Lang Cen's crimes: "Stay still or face extinction!"

sentences.zh: 」種類咸面縛謝過。

translations.literal: " The tribes all bound themselves face-forward and apologized for fault.
translations.idiomatic: They came bound hand and foot to apologize.

sentences.zh: 嶷殺午饗宴，重申恩信。

translations.literal: Ni held a noon feast and banquet, renewing grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He hosted a midday feast to rebuild trust.

sentences.zh: 遂獲鹽鐵，器用周贍。

translations.literal: Thereupon salt and iron were obtained; tools and supplies were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron flowed again and gear grew plentiful.

sentences.zh: 漢嘉郡界旄牛夷種類四千餘戶，其率狼路，欲為姑婿冬逢報怨。

translations.literal: Within Hanjia Commandery more than four thousand households of Maoniu Yi followed chief Lang Lu, wishing to avenge his sister's husband Dong Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand Maoniu households under Lang Lu meant to avenge Dong Feng.

sentences.zh: 遣叔父離將，逢眾相度形勢。

translations.literal: He dispatched his uncle Li to lead Dong Feng's followers to survey the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Lu sent Uncle Li with Dong Feng's men to scout.

sentences.zh: 嶷逆遣親近繼牛酒勞賜，又令離姊逆逢妻宣暢意旨。

translations.literal: Ni in advance sent intimates bearing cattle and wine as gifts and reward, and also ordered Li's elder sister—Dong Feng's wife—to declare his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni preempted him with cattle, wine, and Dong Feng's widow bearing terms.

sentences.zh: 離既受賜，並見其姊，姊弟歡悅，悉率所領將詣嶷，嶷厚加賞待，遣還。

translations.literal: Li having received the gifts and also seen his elder sister, brother and sister rejoiced; they all led those under their command to Ni; Ni richly rewarded and hosted them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Li and his sister accepted; they brought their warriors to Zhang Ni, who feasted them and sent them home reconciled.

sentences.zh: 旄牛由是輒不為患。

translations.literal: Maoniu from this often ceased being a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Maoniu gave little trouble thereafter.

sentences.zh: 郡有舊道，經旄牛中至成都，既平且近。

translations.literal: The commandery had an old road passing through Maoniu territory to Chengdu—level and near.
translations.idiomatic: An ancient highway through Maoniu to Chengdu was straight and easy.

sentences.zh: 自旄牛絕道，已百餘年，更由安上，既險且遠。

translations.literal: Since Maoniu cut the road, over a hundred years had passed; travelers detoured through Anshang—both perilous and distant.
translations.idiomatic: A century of closure forced travelers onto the long Anshang detour.

sentences.zh: 疑遣左右資貨幣賜路，重令路姑喻意，路乃率兄弟妻子悉詣疑，疑與盟誓，開通舊道，千里肅清，復古亭繹。

translations.literal: Ni dispatched attendants bearing goods and coin as gifts to Lang Lu, again charging Lu's aunt to explain his mind; Lu then led brothers, wives, and children all to Ni; Ni swore covenant with them, opened the old road—a thousand li cleared—and restored ancient posts and relays.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni sent gifts and kinswomen to Lang Lu until the chief brought his whole household to swear alliance; the old road reopened with stations restored.

sentences.zh: 奏封路為旋牛毗王，遣使將路朝貢。

translations.literal: He memorialized to enfeoff Lu as king of Maoniu with the title Pi and dispatched envoys to escort Lu to court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Lang Lu as Maoniu king with the Pi title and brought him to Chengdu to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 後主於是加疑撫戎將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: The Later Lord thereupon additionally appointed Ni General Who Pacifies the Rong, retaining concurrent command of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan then named Zhang Ni general who pacifies the Rong while he kept Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 嶷初見費禕為大將軍，恣性泛愛，待信新附不過，嶷書戒之曰：「昔岑彭率師，來歙杖節，咸見害於刺客，今明將軍位尊權重，宜鑒前事，少以為警。

translations.literal: When Ni first saw Fei Yi as Grand General—by nature indulgent and universally fond—his trust of newly submitted men knew no limit—Ni wrote warning him: "Formerly Cen Peng commanded armies and Lai Xi bore credentials—both fell to assassins; now the illustrious general's position is lofty and authority heavy—you ought mirror prior affairs and take slight alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Fei Yi court danger by trusting every newcomer, Zhang Ni cited Cen Peng and Lai Xi: "Great power invites blades—stay wary."

sentences.zh: 」後禕果為魏降人郭脩所害。

translations.literal: " Later Yi was indeed murdered by Wei surrender Guo Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was later killed by the Wei defector Guo Xiu.

sentences.zh: 吳太傅諸葛恪以初破魏軍，大興兵眾以圖攻取。

translations.literal: Wu Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke, because he had newly defeated Wei troops, greatly raised armies and hosts intending to attack and seize.
translations.idiomatic: After beating Wei, Wu's Zhuge Ke mobilized massively for new conquests.

sentences.zh: 侍中諸葛瞻，丞相亮之子，恪從弟也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhuge Zhan—Chancellor Liang's son—was Ke's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhuge Zhan—Zhuge Liang's son—was Zhuge Ke's cousin.

sentences.zh: 嶷與書曰：

translations.literal: Ni wrote to him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni wrote Zhuge Zhan:

sentences.zh: 東主初崩，帝實幼弱，太傅受寄託之重，亦何容易！

translations.literal: The eastern lord has newly died; the emperor is truly young and weak; the Grand Tutor bears heavy testamentary charge—how can it be easy!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang is a boy and Zhuge Ke shoulders regency—no light burden.

sentences.zh: 親以周公之才，猶有管、蔡流言之變，霍光受任，亦有燕、蓋、上官逆亂之謀，賴成、昭之明，以免斯難耳。

translations.literal: Even with the Duke of Zhou's talents there were still the Guan and Cai rumor disasters; Huo Guang accepted mandate yet still faced Yan, Gai, and Shangguan rebellious plots—only relying on Emperors Cheng and Zhao's clarity escaped such hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou faced Guan-Cai slander; Huo Guang survived Yan and Shangguan plots—only sage young rulers saved them.

sentences.zh: 昔每聞東主殺生賞罰，不任下人，又今以垂沒之命，卒召太傅，屬以後事，誠實可慮。

translations.literal: Formerly each time I heard the eastern lord on killing and sparing rewards and punishments did not delegate to subordinates; moreover now with dying breath he suddenly summoned the Grand Tutor and entrusted later affairs—it truly warrants worry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan micromanaged justice to the end; handing regency from a deathbed is doubly tense.

sentences.zh: 加吳、楚剽急，乃昔所記，而太傅離少主，履敵庭，恐非良計長算之術也。

translations.literal: Add that Wu and Chu are rash by nature—as recorded of old—and the Grand Tutor leaves the young lord and treads the enemy court; I fear this is no skillful long calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu temper is famously rash; leaving the boy emperor for Wei battlefields seems unsound.

sentences.zh: 雖云東家綱紀肅然，上下輯睦，百有一失，非明者之慮邪？

translations.literal: Although they say the eastern house's discipline is stern and high and low harmonize—if one slip occurs in a hundred, is it not what the enlightened must consider?
translations.idiomatic: Even orderly Wu can err once in a hundred tries—should not the wise hedge?"

sentences.zh: 取古則今，今則古也，自非郎君進忠言於太傅，誰復有盡言者也！

translations.literal: Taking antiquity as mirror for today and today for antiquity—if not you, sir, advancing loyal words to the Grand Tutor, who again will speak exhaustively!
translations.idiomatic: History mirrors the present—only you can speak plainly to your cousin."

sentences.zh: 旋軍廣農，務行德惠，數年之中，東西並舉，實為不晚，願深採察。

translations.literal: Withdraw troops, broaden agriculture, diligently practice virtue and kindness—within several years strike east and west together; truly it is not late—please deeply adopt and examine.
translations.idiomatic: Disband hosts, farm, build virtue—strike later when odds improve."

sentences.zh: 恪竟以此夷族。

translations.literal: Ke in the end for this was exterminated clan-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke ignored him and died with his whole lineage.

sentences.zh: 嶷識見多如是類。

translations.literal: Ni's insight and judgment were often of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni read men and moments often thus.

sentences.zh: 在郡十五年，邦域安穆。

translations.literal: Fifteen years in the commandery—the domain was secure and calm.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen quiet years in Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 屢乞求還，乃徵詣成都。

translations.literal: Repeatedly begging to return, he was at last summoned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He begged recall until Chengdu summoned him.

sentences.zh: 夷民戀慕，扶轂泣涕，過旄牛邑，邑君襁負來迎，及追尋至蜀郡界，其督相率隨嶷朝貢者百餘人。

translations.literal: Yi commoners clung to him, supporting his carriage hubs and weeping; passing Maoniu town the town lord carried infants to greet him; chasing all the way to Shu Commandery border, more than a hundred chiefs followed Ni to court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes clung to his wheels, infants met him at Maoniu, and a hundred chiefs escorted him toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 嶷至，拜蕩寇將軍，慷慨壯烈，士人咸多貴之。

translations.literal: When Ni arrived he was appointed General Who Sweeps Away Bandits—spirited and heroic—gentlemen all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu named him general who sweeps away bandits; literati admired his fire.

sentences.zh: 然放蕩少禮，人亦以此譏焉，

translations.literal: Yet he was unrestrained and short on ritual—people also mocked him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt manners drew ridicule.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：時車騎將軍夏侯霸謂嶷曰：「雖與足下疏闊，然託心如舊，宜明此意。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Ni: "Although with you, sir, I am distant and broad, yet my heart entrusts as of old—you ought clarify this intent.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xiahou Ba told Zhang Ni he wished old ties renewed.〉

sentences.zh: 」嶷答曰：「僕未知子，子未知我，大道在彼，何云託心乎！

translations.literal: " Ni replied: "Your servant does not know you, sir; you do not know me—the great Way lies yonder—what speak of entrusting hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ni answered coldly: "We hardly know each other—talk of hearts is premature."

sentences.zh: 原三年之後徐陳斯言。

translations.literal: I beg after three years slowly to state these words.
translations.idiomatic: Let three years pass before such intimacy."

sentences.zh: 」有識之士以為美談。〉

translations.literal: " Men of discernment considered this fine conversation.〉
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men praised the exchange.〉

sentences.zh: 是歲延熙十七年也。

translations.literal: That year was the seventeenth year of Yanxi [254].
translations.idiomatic: It was 254.

sentences.zh: 魏狄道長李簡密書請降，衛將軍姜維率嶷等因簡之資以出隴西。

translations.literal: Wei Didao county chief Li Jian secretly wrote requesting surrender; Guard General Jiang Wei led Ni and others using Jian's resources to issue forth into Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Didao magistrate Li Jian plotted defection; Jiang Wei exploited it to march into Longxi with Zhang Ni.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷風濕固疾，至都浸篤，扶杖然後能起。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Ni's rheumatic ailment was chronic; reaching the capital it worsened—only with a staff could he rise.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Chronic rheumatism crippled him in Chengdu.〉

sentences.zh: 李簡請降，眾議狐疑，而嶷曰必然。

translations.literal: When Li Jian sought surrender the assembly doubted; Ni said it was certain.
translations.idiomatic: Court skeptics doubted Li Jian; Zhang Ni insisted it was genuine.

sentences.zh: 姜維之出，時論以嶷初還，股疾不能在行中，由是嶷自乞肆力中原，致身敵庭。

translations.literal: When Jiang Wei marched forth, contemporary opinion held that Ni had just returned and leg ailment kept him from the column—thereby Ni himself begged to exert strength in the Central Plains and give his body to the enemy court.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill from travel he volunteered for Jiang Wei's western thrust anyway.

sentences.zh: 臨發，辭後主曰：「臣當值聖明，受恩過量，加以疾病在身，常恐一朝隕沒，辜負榮遇。

translations.literal: As he was about to set out, taking leave of the Later Lord he said: 'Your servant has encountered sagely clarity and received favor beyond measure; added to that sickness afflicts my body—I constantly fear falling dead one morning and betraying this splendid encounter.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching he told Liu Shan: “I have enjoyed imperial favor beyond merit and bear a sickly frame—I dread dying overnight and failing your trust.”

sentences.zh: 天不違原，得豫戎事。

translations.literal: Heaven did not thwart my prayer; I was able to take part in martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven granted my wish to join the campaign.”

sentences.zh: 若涼州克定，臣為籓表守將；

translations.literal: If Liangzhou is conquered and settled, your servant will be a frontier-screen guarding commander on the outer defense;
translations.idiomatic: If we secure Liangzhou I will hold the frontier for you;

sentences.zh: 若有未捷，殺身以報。

translations.literal: If there is no victory, I will kill myself to repay.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I give my life in repayment.”

sentences.zh: 」後主慨然為之流涕。〉

translations.literal: ' The Later Lord sighed deeply and for him shed tears.〉
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan wept at his words.〉

sentences.zh: 既到狄道，簡悉率城中吏民出迎軍。

translations.literal: When they reached Didao, Jian led all clerks and commoners of the city out to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Didao, Li Jian brought the whole town out to greet Jiang Wei’s host.

sentences.zh: 軍前與魏將徐質交鋒，嶷臨陣隕身，然其所殺傷亦過倍。

translations.literal: Before the army he crossed blades with Wei general Xu Zhi; Ni fell in facing battle—yet those he killed and wounded were also more than double.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Xu Zhi at the front and died in action after inflicting more than twice his own losses.

sentences.zh: 既亡，封長子瑛西鄉侯，次子護雄襲爵。

translations.literal: After his death, his eldest son Ying was enfeoffed Marquis of Xixiang; second son Huguo succeeded to the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously his eldest son Zhang Ying became marquis of Xixiang and his second son Zhang Huguo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 南土越崔巂民夷聞嶷死，無不悲泣，為嶷立廟，四時水旱輒祀之。

translations.literal: People of the southern lands—the Han and Yi of Yuexi Commandery—hearing of Ni's death, none did not weep in sorrow; they erected a temple for Ni; at the four seasons for flood or drought they always sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Han and Yi of Yuexi wept at Zhang Ni’s death, built him shrines, and prayed there whenever drought or flood struck.

sentences.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：余觀張嶷儀貌辭令，不能駭人，而其策略足以入算，果烈足以立威，為臣有忠誠之節，處類有亮直之風，而動必顧典，後主深崇之。

translations.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: I observed Zhang Ni—his bearing and speech could not startle people, yet his stratagems sufficed to enter calculation; his decisive fierceness sufficed to establish awe; as minister he had integrity of loyalty; among peers he had the wind of candid straightness; yet in action he always consulted the canon—the Later Lord deeply revered him.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yibu tradition says Zhang Ni looked unremarkable yet planned brilliantly, fought fiercely, served with steadfast loyalty, stood candid among colleagues, and weighed every act against precedent—so Liu Shan revered him deeply.”

sentences.zh: 雖古之英士，何以遠逾哉！

translations.literal: Although compared to ancient heroic gentlemen—how could they surpass him far!
translations.idiomatic: Ancient heroes would scarcely surpass him!”

sentences.zh: 《蜀世譜》曰：嶷孫奕，晉梁州刺史。〉

translations.literal: The Shu Shifu states: Ni's grandson Yi was Liang Province Inspector of Jin.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Shu shifu adds that Zhang Ni’s grandson Zhang Yi became Jin’s inspector of Liangzhou.〉

sentences.zh: 【評價】

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: 【Closing appraisal】

sentences.zh: 評曰：黃權弘雅思量，李恢公亮志業，呂凱守節不回，馬忠擾而能毅，

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Huang Quan was magnanimous and cultivated in capacity; Li Hui was fair and bright in aspiration and enterprise; Lü Kai guarded integrity without turning back; Ma Zhong was yielding yet able to be resolute—
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou judged Huang Quan broad-minded, Li Hui steadfastly honest, Lü Kai incorruptible, Ma Zhong supple yet firm,

sentences.zh: 〈《尚書》曰：擾而毅。

translations.literal: 〈The Document states: yielding yet resolute.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The *Shangshu* line runs “pliant yet resolute.”

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注曰：擾，馴也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: yielding means tame.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses *rao* as “trainable” or “pliant.”

sentences.zh: 致果曰毅。〉

translations.literal: Achieving decisive fruit is called resolute.〉
translations.idiomatic: Decisive valor is what *yi* names.〉

sentences.zh: 王平忠勇而嚴整，張嶷識斷明果，咸以所長，顯名發跡，遇其時也。

translations.literal: Wang Ping was loyal and brave yet sternly ordered; Zhang Ni's judgment was clear and decisive—all by their strengths displayed fame and rose to traces—meeting their season.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping paired loyalty with discipline; Zhang Ni paired insight with bold action—each rose because the age demanded his gifts.
